articles.title: Sony Explores Unconventional Release and Box Office Strategy for Beatles Biopics
articles.summary: ony Pictures is mulling a few different novel release strategies for director Sam Mendes’ The Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event, from releasing all four films on the same day in April 2028 to lumping the box office returns of all four films together so that no one Beatle biopic can be deemed more successful than the other.
articles.body:
Sony Pictures is mulling a few different novel release strategies for director Sam Mendes’ The Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event , from releasing all four films on the same day in April 2028 to lumping the box office returns of all four films together so that no one Beatle biopic can be deemed more successful than the other.

According to sources for The Hollywood Reporter , the studio and Mendes “have long mulled dropping all four movies the same day. In addition, Mendes and the studio have been pondering a highly unique reporting structure for the films’ box office receipts. Instead of releasing each film’s tally individually, the studio has been considering lumping the returns of all four movies together.”

Sony may also offer filmgoers a four-pack of tickets to the entire quartet of films, but that would require theater chains to figure out how exactly to sell that to filmgoers.

THR adds: “Assuming all four movies do indeed drop the same week, sources also say the plan is to market the films as not having a particular order — that there will be no ‘right’ order in which to watch the films.”

The Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event

What Sony hopes to avoid is a scenario where audiences are seen to prefer any one member of the Fab Four over the other, where maybe most filmgoers go to see the John Lennon or Paul McCartney movie and wait for streaming to watch the George Harrison or Ringo Starr ones.

Pippa Harris, one of the films’ producers, recently spoke at the BFI London Film Festival ’s Industry Forum where she said the filmmakers and studio “want people to be able to experience them in the cinema at the same time, during the same period. … Now that doesn’t necessarily mean we’re thinking that people will go and see all four films on the same day. But within the same month, you might see one a week, or you might see one film one weekend and another the next.”

Saoirse Ronan plays Linda McCartney, Anna Sawai plays Yoko Ono, Aimee Lou Wood plays Pattie Boyd, Mia McKenna-Bruce plays Maureen Starkey, David Morrissey plays Paul McCartney’s father Jim McCartney, Leanne Best plays John Lennon’s Aunt Mimi, James Norton plays their manager Brian Epstein, Harry Lloyd plays music producer George Martin, Bobby Schofield plays road manager and confidant Neil Aspinall, Daniel Hoffman-Gill plays roadie Mal Evans, Arthur Darvill plays press officer Derek Taylor, and Adam Pally plays music manager Allen Klein.

articles.title: In 1994, Samuel L. Jackson’s ‘Pulp Fiction’ was released; 32 years later, the 77-year-old actor still remembers his iconic speech
articles.summary: In a heartfelt tribute to the iconic film Pulp Fiction, Samuel L. Jackson shares a video reciting his memorable Ezekiel 25:17 speech, celebrating 32 years of the movie's enduring legacy.
articles.body: Some movie scenes stay with audiences long after the credits roll, and Samuel L. Jackson is a memorable reminder of why his performance in ‘Pulp Fiction’ continues to stand out. 32 years after Quentin Tarantino’s 1994 crime drama reached theatres, Jackson has returned to one of its most recognisable moments, showing that the dialogue is still firmly in his memory.The 77-year-old actor marked the film’s anniversary on October 14, 2026, by sharing a video on his official Instagram account. In the clip, he recites the famous speech associated with his character, Jules Winnfield, the hitman whose intimidating delivery became one of the film’s defining scenes. The video offered fans a chance to revisit a performance that helped establish Jackson as one of Hollywood’s most distinctive screen presences.Samuel L. Jackson remembers his famous ‘Pulp Fiction’ speechJackson shared the video with a caption that made his confidence clear. He wrote, “32 years later, I still got this one on lock!!! #pulpfiction.”The post was a celebration of both the film and a character that remains closely associated with Jackson’s career. His recitation revisits the speech commonly identified as Ezekiel 25:17, delivered by Jules in a tense scene involving a man named Brett. The monologue begins with a reflection on righteousness and evil before building towards its famous declaration of vengeance.Samuel L. Jackson’s delivery helped turn the scene into one of the film’s most talked-about moments. The speech is not simply remembered for its words; the actor’s controlled expression, commanding voice and sudden shifts in intensity make it difficult to forget.His latest video also shows how a performance from decades ago can continue to connect with viewers. Fans who remember watching the film in theatres can revisit the scene, while newer audiences can discover why Jules Winnfield remains such a recognisable character.Why does Jules Winnfield remain one of his most memorable roles?Released in 1994, ‘Pulp Fiction’ was directed by Quentin Tarantino and featured an ensemble cast including John Travolta, Uma Thurman, Bruce Willis, Ving Rhames, Tim Roth and Harvey Keitel. The film follows several interconnected crime stories in Los Angeles, presenting them through a non-linear narrative.Samuel L. Jackson played Jules Winnfield alongside Travolta’s Vincent Vega. The two portray hitmen whose conversations and encounters give the film much of its distinctive rhythm.The Ezekiel 25:17 speech captures the character at his most threatening, but its significance extends beyond intimidation. It becomes part of Jules’ changing relationship with violence and the possibility of choosing another path.The film received seven Academy Award nominations at the 1995 Oscars. Jackson earned his first Academy Award nomination for his performance in the Best Supporting Actor category, while Tarantino and Roger Avary won for Original Screenplay.‘Pulp Fiction’ continues to hold a special place in cinemaThe film’s influence has lasted well beyond its original theatrical run. Its unusual storytelling structure, memorable dialogue and mix of dark humour and violence helped make it a defining title of 1990s cinema.For Jackson, the anniversary also offers an opportunity to revisit a role that became an important part of his screen legacy. His career has since included major performances in films such as ‘Jackie Brown’, ‘Django Unchained’ and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, where he plays Nick Fury.In April 2024, Samuel L. Jackson got back together with his ‘Pulp Fiction’ co-stars John Travolta and Uma Thurman in Los Angeles to celebrate 30 years of the film. The gathering gave the cast and fans another opportunity to celebrate the movie’s lasting impact.Two years later, Jackson’s anniversary video has brought the conversation back to a single performance. His ability to recall the speech decades after filming highlights the lasting connection between an actor and a character that audiences continue to remember.The film may be 32 years old, but Jules Winnfield’s words remain familiar to generations of movie fans.
